newsitem.title: SPAIN: Spain king to make rare address after ETA killing.
newsitem.headline: Spain king to make rare address after ETA killing.

text.p: Spain's King Juan Carlos will make a rare address to the nation on Monday night condemning the kidnap and brutal killing of a young politician by Basque separatists, state television said.

The king will speak to the nation on television and radio at 7.45 p.m. (1745 GMT), 15 minutes before a huge demonstration led by Prime Minister Jose Maria Aznar is scheduled to begin in central Madrid.
The king sent his son Crown Prince Felipe to the funeral of town councillor Miguel Angel Blanco in the Basque town of Ermua on Monday.

The king has rarely addressed the nation apart from his regular speech at Christmas. In 1981, the king made a speech after military officers stormed parliament and held legislators hostage in an attempted coup.
The public street protest in Madrid after the coup was the largest in Spanish history. Officials say the demonstration in Madrid on Monday could reach similar proportions.

Blanco, 29, was killed after ETA rebels kidnapped him and demanded the government move about 500 ETA inmates to the Basque region before 4 p.m on Saturday. He was found bound with two gunshot wounds in his head shortly after the deadline on Saturday and died some 12 hours later.
